ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Acting City Manager Toney discussed City operations and response to Palisades
  Fire. He announced that City Hall is open by appointment only and appointments
  can be scheduled via email or phone. He stated staff was working on plans for a
  permanent rebuild office in a building adjacent to City Hall. He stated more
  information was available at malibucity.org/palisadesflre and encouraged the
  public to sign up for e-notifications. He cautioned the public to be vigilant about
  scams following disasters.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Acting City Manager Toney discussed staffing plans
  and plans to bring on consultants to support rebuilding. He stated the City had
  positive momentum on recruitments before the fires.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, expressed
  sympathy for everyone who was impacted by the Palisades Fire. He discussed the
  department’s response to the Palisades Fire and Eaton Fire and the Deputies’
  dedicated service. He announced there was an additional fatality from the Palisades
  Fire. He discussed dangerous conditions on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) after
  the fire and stated the road would be open to residents only. He announced resident
  passes would be distributed from 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. at City Hall beginning
  tomorrow. He stated contractors and essential personnel could obtain access passes
  at the Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Sergeant Soderlund stated essential personnel would
  be considered on a case by case basis.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Sergeant Soderlund stated businesses in the
  bum area were not open and access was resident only.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund stated the pass
  could not be transferred and would only be issued to residents with address
  verification.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Sergeant Soderlund stated the Sheriff’s Department
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 27, 2025
  Page 6 of 15

  was meeting with Caltrans every day to discuss PCH.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins discussed the long-term traffic impacts of the fire on PCH.

  Mayor Stewart discussed the construction on PCH.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund stated access to the
  road could not limited only to Malibu residents once it reopened.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Sergeant Soderlund stated the checkpoint
  for the road closure would be at the 22500 block of PCH.

RECESS  At 6:15 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:32
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Julie Swisher, Red Cross, thanked the Council for its support. She discussed red

  Marissa Coughlan commended Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy for

  Joseph Lezama discussed his work with property owners, architects and developers
  on navigating the Coastal Development Permit process. He asked how the City
  Hall appointments differed from counter hours and what services were available.

  previously destroyed in the 1993 fire. He discussed his experience rebuilding after
  the 1993 fire. He recommended the City work with local professionals who had

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins expressed condolences for everyone in the community
  impacted by the Palisades Fire. She thanked City staff for their service during the
  fire and thanked the City of Westlake Village, City of Camarillo, and Pepperdine
  University for hosting the City’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC). She
  thanked the partner agencies that sent staff to support the EOC, local volunteers,
  Los Angeles County Fire Department, other fire crews that responded to the fire,
  Los Angeles County Sheriff’ s Department, the National Guard, the Red Cross, and
  the Malibu Boys and Girls Club for their response to the fire. She discussed the
  importance of supporting the business community. She addressed several logistical
  issues related to recovery. She clarified that the cost of debris removal would
  depend on the individual property and structure. While the federal government
  covers the opt-in option, insurance holders may be asked to sign over their debris
  coverage. She explained that the additional 10% for like-for—like rebuilds is in the
  City’s Local Coastal Program, and anyone wanting to expand further would need
  to go through a separate permitting process. She stated that the Sheriff’s
  Department has deployed surveillance tools like drones and infrared systems in the
  mountains to enhance safety. She encouraged residents with surviving homes to
  take advantage of free home hardening inspections offered by the City and
  Community Brigade to increase future fire resilience. In response to questions
  about septic tanks, she explained that damage assessments would need to be
  conducted by professionals and systems may require replacement. She discussed
  the unprecedented scale of the disaster and stated federal and local agencies are
  working hard to speed up recovery.

  Councilmember Conrad thanked the first responders, second responders, and the
  Malibu community. She inquired if the City had been in contact with the Chumash
  tribe. She requested townhall meetings with Southern California Edison and
  Caltrans. She expressed her dedication to rebuilding and improving the rebuild
  process. She requested more information on the OTS funding. She indicated
  support for permitting pools as a means of increasing fire protection. She discussed
  communication failures during the fire and expressed interest in exploring a
  warning siren system. She expressed concern that the Mayor appointed a
  representative to the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy Advisory Board
  without consulting the Council.

  Mayor Stewart clarified that Brian Merrick had been designated to represent the
  City on a temporary basis after the City’s representative Lloyd Ahern was
  hospitalized after the fire.

  Councilmember Conrad discussed the importance of supporting small businesses

  Councilmember Silverstein stated California law allowed those who lose their
  homes in a wildfire to purchase a new house with their insurance payout. He
  discussed the City’s active emergency declarations and the additional powers the

  remediation requirements for 4000 Malibu Canyon Road. He discussed the
  importance of getting students additional support after the loss of so many

  Councilmember Uhring announced the debris removal right of entry form had been
  published ahead of schedule.

Lg  Councilmember Conrad stated the Community Brigades was receiving $750,000 in

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a
  motion to: 1) adopt Resolution No. 25-06 initiating a Local Coastal Program (LCP)
  amendment and zoning text amendment to consider changes to the Malibu LCP and
  Title 17 (Zoning) of the Malibu Municipal Code (MMC) to facilitate the rebuilding
